notes:
Summary: mid-market B2B product analytics company experimenting with LLM-powered in-app assistant + search. Ran a 30-day hosted API trial Jan-Feb 2026. Wants Dedicated after proving unit economics and predictable latency.

Trial metrics (hosted API):
- Average QPS: 2.3 req/s across trial (non-peak).
- Peak sustained QPS: 12 req/s during Monday morning syncs (observed 10x baseline).
- Typical concurrency (active websocket streams): 6 concurrent chat sessions; spikes to 28 during release notes send.
- Token mix: ~40% short prompts (10-40 tokens), 50% chat exchanges (avg 180 prompt + 220 completion tokens), 10% long-batch embeddings (median 512 tokens).
- Avg token size per request: ~280 tokens.
- 95th p99 latency (hosted): 420ms server-side for small chat completions, 1.2s for long generation paths. Target for production: sub-300ms for short-inference paths, sub-800ms for long flows.
- Model preference: open models with strong throughput (Llama 2 variants, quantized FP16), interested in Redwood-verified m models with fallback to smaller quantized versions for cost control.

Use-case detail:
- Primary: in-product conversational assistant that summarizes user account activity and answers product questions (chat + summarization).
- Secondary: embeddings for semantic search across docs and support articles (batch & incremental); reranking for search results.
- QPS profile: spikey (daily peaks), predictable weekly cadence, occasional monthly spikes tied to product launches.
- Cost sensitivity: medium-high — unit cost must be predictable; willing to commit to reserved capacity if ROI is 2x cost savings vs hosted.

POC/Demo history:
- 2026-01-06: kickoff call (ff_2026-01-06_1015) — scoped objectives and SLAs.
- 2026-01-11: demo: streaming chat + tool calling.
- 2026-02-08: hosted trial starts (30 days).
- 2026-02-22: mid-trial check-in — adjusted batching params per Redwood Optimize suggestions (see drive calc).
- 2026-03-01: trial wrap call — shared metrics, engineering asked for Dedicated sizing guidance.

Engineering asks / requirements:
- Dedicated capacity recommendation with: expected QPS handling, concurrent KV cache sizing, token-per-second throughput per GPU, and burst capacity plan.
- Guidance on batching windows, prefix caching for repeated user queries, and model quantization tradeoffs.
- SLA targets: 99.9% availability, p95 latency targets per route.
- Security: SSO/SAML for SREs, audit logs retention 1 year, KMS integration for keys, SOC2 report for vendor.

Commercial / procurement notes:
- Interested in 12-month reserved plan if Redwood provides a pricing credit based on committed QPS and a fallback policy for overage.
- Procurement: legal needs DPA + security questionnaire returned before PO. Finance prefers invoiced quarterly.

Next steps (short):
- Redwood to deliver Dedicated capacity calc (spreadsheet) by 2026-03-10 (Rashmi to own).
- Maya to schedule pricing review with Finance week of 2026-03-15.
- Security: Jordan to share SOC2 artifact; Sunboard legal to return DPA by 2026-03-22.
